evidence: .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/instruction.md:1 opens with "Can you build me a polished full-stack operations app for HireOps" and identifies the recruiting/compensation user. Line 3 narrates opening a requisition, composing compensation, approval, revisions and rescission, and explains why the figures must be visible (the team argues about them and currently calculates them by hand). Lines 5 and 11 tie navigation, persistent audit history and repeated revisions to everyday use. The eight prose paragraphs contain no numbered acceptance list, feature matrix, shall/must table or ordered implementation recipe. Line 9 is a dense runtime paragraph, but its Node/Express/SQLite, entry, port, storage, health and network constraints correspond to the frozen template integration.md:3-14; it expressly leaves other files and routes to the implementer. Line 7 delegates detailed operating rules to the public notes rather than transcribing their tables into the brief. Adversarial reading: a broken static dashboard that merely has the six screen names and the health endpoint could satisfy isolated nouns, but cannot satisfy the stated real backend, approval commitment, revision/rescission and persistent-history journey at lines 1, 3, 5 and 11. Conversely, a conforming app may use different non-health routes, file organization and screen layouts without contradicting this ask (line 9 and hireops_rules.md, "A note on what is here"); no implementation sequence is demanded. This assesses prompt form only, not whether the scoring rubric catches that broken app. Direct SHA256 checks matched the frozen manifest for the nine cited frozen task/rule/template files and four policy/context files; instruction.md is 8ff0f4a1575b84ca35f561db7bbe51855e566aebea2582897970277acff7b361, workbook is 6d44970b2ff67fefad1e2327e743fc226fcd4c50ff55baf899f41069a9b3fd7f, and recomputing the canonical inputs digest matched the assigned input_sha256. No app runtime or provider measurement is needed for this textual row, and none is claimed.
